blocks.label: Definition
blocks.html: The range is the difference between the largest and smallest values: Range = Maximum − Minimum.

blocks.label: Simplified Explanation
blocks.html: The crudest answer to “how spread out is this?” is to subtract the smallest value from the largest. It gives the span the data cover and says nothing about how values are arranged inside that span.

blocks.label: Illustration / Example
blocks.html:
Weights of five children: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 kg → range = 13 − 9 = 4 kg. A different five children: 9, 11, 11, 11, 13 → range is still 4 kg, although these values cluster tightly at 11 apart from the two ends. The range uses only 2 of the n values.

Today’s 30 children (recall §1.4.1) run from 8.6 to 15.3 kg: range = 6.7 kg.

points.html: Simple, but it uses only the two extremes, so a single outlier changes it completely, and it tends to grow as the sample grows (more chances to catch an extreme value).
Useful as a first data check: an age range of “−5 to 200 years” flags an entry error at once. It is rarely the main reported measure of spread in research.
